text.p: Here are highlights of stories in the Romanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- The State Ownership Fund (FPS) started liquidation of 20 loss-making pig and poultry farms.
- Romanian state television earned only 39 billion lei from selling air time in 1996, although its ratings still exceed those of private commercial televisions.
- Some 30 percent of Romania's 1996 ready-mades production -- worth 1.33 trillion lei -- is sold on the domestic market.
- High income taxes force employers to pay low wages.
BURSA
- Currency exchange bureaux and the black market were drained of lei, while the dollar-leu rate dropped constantly in the past 10 days.
ADEVARUL
- Prices of Romanian-made medicine doubled.

- Industry ministry made a list of 32 key factories -- including steel-mills in Galati, Calarasi and Tirgoviste and farm machinery manufaturers Tractorul Brasov SA and Semanatoarea Bucuresti SA -- to be privatised shortly.
- Fuel traders sell their diesel abroad, due to shortages of funds for farmers to buy it for the spring campaign.
- Hotels remain empty after prices soared in line with recent tourism ministry liberalisation measures.
- Romania should set up a special "banking police" to prevent money laundering, said senator Varujan Vosganian, head of parliament's banking and finance commission.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- State-owned Bancorex SA bank raised its share capital to 1.19 trillion lei from a previous 93 billion, after a cabinet decision to increase the face value of a share to 1.8 million lei from 140,000 previously.
- Romania will borrow some 250,000 tonnes of milling wheat for bread consumption and return the amount from the 1997 crop, Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu told a parliament farming commission.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- A delegation of the French car maker Renault arrived in Romania to analyse prospects of resuming cooperation with local manufacturer Dacia Pitesti SA and to look into new partners.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- German Chancellor Helmuth Kohl is expected to make a visit to Romania in the second half of 1997.
- The Romanian community living in the U.S. will start lobby campaign for Romania's admission to NATO. They will write 10,000 letters to the White House and to Congressmen.
- Romanians smuggle sheep over the border to Serbia.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Food prices started to go down because Romanians don't have money to buy the products, the newspaper says.
- Bucharest court of appeals ruled that coal miners' leader Miron Cosma remain in jail pending investigations on suspicions of undermining state authority during miners' riots in 1991.
ADEVARUL
- Romania is the only East European country which does not have a law against money laundering.
- Romania has 50 percent chances to join NATO, said Jonathan Eyal, head of the London-based Royal Institute for Strategic Studies.
- Health ministry set at 60,000 lei tariffs for abortions. Single women who earn less than 300,000 lei per month can have free abortions.
- A Bucharest military court will start on Friday a trial against colonel Gheorghe Marinescu, charged with instigation to murder during the 1989 revolution.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Spain clearly expressed its support for Romania's bid to win quick NATO entry, Senate chairman Petre Roman said after his visit to Spain. ($= 7,744 lei) -- Bucharest newsroom 40-1 3120264
